description: Cooks every Sunday and keeps making dishes. Studies Japanese on their own, chose a Japanese history elective to understand the culture, watches anime and wants to visit Kyoto. Has three side projects.
tests: When one topic shows up repeatedly across different contexts (self-study, elective class, anime, travel), the topic-level generalization IS allowed. Guards against being so cautious that nothing is promoted
A clear self-statement ("I cook every Sunday... it's my reset") is promoted after one mention
Dishes are appended as separate records, not merged into one sentence
"Yesterday" in a message dated 9/13 is recorded as 9/12
Three projects mentioned once are grouped as records under one projects category; the robot arm's progress is appended

observations.note: Made shakshuka with cumin and a little feta on the morning of 2026-09-06.
Says they cook every Sunday and use chopping vegetables to clear their head and reset for the week.
observations.hook: Repetitive hands-on preparation as a way to clear their head and reset for the week.
observations.quote: I cook every Sunday no matter what. It's my reset for the week, chopping vegetables just clears my head.

observations.note: Usually decides what to cook that morning based on what is available in the fridge.
observations.hook: Deciding spontaneously based on ingredients already available.
observations.quote: Usually decide that morning based on whatever's in the fridge.

observations.note: Made shoyu ramen from scratch with chicken; the broth took seven hours, and the tare was the hardest part.
observations.quote: Made ramen from scratch yesterday. Took me 7 hours for the broth lol

observations.note: Has been studying Japanese on Duolingo for about three months and says they chose to learn it without being asked.
observations.hook: Choosing to learn something voluntarily, without an external assignment
observations.quote: Nobody asked me to learn it, I just wanted to.

observations.note: While making ramen, was able to read some of the soy sauce bottle label using Japanese they had been learning, and felt proud of that.
observations.hook: Noticing a practiced skill help with an everyday real-world task
observations.caveat: Could read only some of the label.

observations.note: Asked on their own initiative about how sakoku affected food and whether sushi originated in that era, despite noting the topic was not on the syllabus.
observations.hook: Tracing how historical policies shaped everyday food and its origins
observations.quote: This isn't on the syllabus, but how did that affect what people ate in Edo? Did sushi come from that era?

observations.note: Said they chose the elective to understand the culture behind food and a language they are interested in.
observations.hook: Understanding the cultural context behind food and language
observations.quote: I picked this elective because I wanted to understand the culture behind the food and the language I'm into.

observations.note: Reacted that sushi being described as fast food was funny.
observations.hook: The unexpected framing of familiar sushi as fast food
observations.quote: Sushi as fast food is so funny.

observations.note: The student said they were sad after finishing Frieren; they did not specify what about it drew them in.
The student said temple scenes in anime consistently appeal to them.
observations.hook: The portrayal of temple settings in fictional scenes
observations.quote: the temple scenes in anime always get me.

observations.note: The student wants to visit Kyoto someday, possibly next year, and is saving for the trip.
observations.hook: Seeing Kyoto temple settings connected to scenes in anime
observations.quote: I really want to go to Kyoto someday

observations.note: The student said they are saving up for a Kyoto trip.
observations.caveat: They said the trip might be next year.
